sections.content: How many people stayed in Annfield Plain after gaining qualifications?

Annfield Plain is a small town in the North East. Annfield Plain does not have its own university.

Annfield Plain has higher levels of deprivation.

Overall, Annfield Plain ended up with:

  • a similar number of graduates as it produced
  • more non-graduates with advanced qualifications than it produced
Note: all towns and cities in this analysis are defined based on population size only. This means that some cities are classed as towns because of their population.

Let's explore this further

There were 470 state-school pupils from Annfield Plain who sat their GCSEs between the 2007 to 2008 and the 2010 to 2011 school years.

Of these, 90 (19%) went on to gain degree-level qualifications (level 6+ as defined by The Office of Qualifications and Examinations Regulation, or Ofqual ). We will call these people graduates.

Another 180 (38%) went on to gain other advanced post-16 qualifications, such as A-Levels, a foundation degree or higher apprenticeship (levels 3-5 as defined by Ofqual). In this tool, we will refer to these non-graduates with advanced qualifications as “qualified non-graduates", for brevity.

The charts below compare Annfield Plain to other English towns and cities using three measures:

  • what proportion of Annfield Plain's pupils became graduates or qualified non-graduates by the 2017 to 2018 academic year
  • of those graduates and qualified non-graduates, the percentages that lived in Annfield Plain in the 2018 to 2019 academic year
  • how many graduates and qualified non-graduates from elsewhere came to live there by 2018 to 2019, relative to the number who sat their GCSEs there

In some towns, some of this information may not be available because of small sample sizes.
The size and deprivation level of a town, as well as the qualification levels of older residents, were all related to students' educational attainment. Read our previous analysis.

In 2018 to 2019, 42% of graduates and 38% of qualified non-graduates living in Annfield Plain had moved there from elsewhere

In the 2018 to 2019 academic year, there were 95 graduates and 200 qualified (level 3+) non-graduates from our cohort living in Annfield Plain. This is compared with the 90 graduates and 180 qualified non-graduates who had lived there when they sat their GCSEs.

In 2018 to 2019, 63% of the graduates had also lived in Annfield Plain as GCSE pupils, while 42% had moved there from elsewhere.

Of the qualified non-graduates who lived in Annfield Plain in 2018 to 2019, 63% had lived there as GCSE pupils, while 38% had moved to the area from elsewhere.
